parents.title: Rate of radius decay determines analytic versus entire densities

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: The decisive condition is that the phase radii do not become too small too quickly. If the inverse radii grow at most linearly, sufficiently many nontrivial one-coordinate Fourier factors yield some exponential transform decay and hence real analyticity of both limiting densities. If inverse-radius growth is sublinear, the proof obtains arbitrarily strong exponential decay and hence entire extension. Smaller radii weaken individual factors, so the mechanism is the availability of many sufficiently large radii—not 'faster input decay buys more analyticity.'
